findings.title: Unbounded raster amplification in PDF ingestion: MuPDF renders the full page surface with no page-count, byte-size or page-dimension cap
findings.description: The PDF ingestion path opens operator- or third-party-supplied PDFs and renders pages to rasters proportional to page dimensions before any repo-side size gate, so a sub-kilobyte hostile PDF can force hundreds of megabytes of allocation. Measured: an 819-byte PDF with a 6000x6000pt MediaBox drove a 496 KB pixmap and ~509 MB RSS growth (606x amplification); 275x at 4000pt, 77x at 2000pt.
findings.claimed_root_cause: pdf_conv_md opens the source PDF and the engine chain (pdf_local born-digital, liteparse OCR, teleocr scanned render) materializes page rasters via page.get_pixmap(matrix) with no MAX_PAGES, MAX_INPUT_BYTES or MAX_PAGE_PTS cap anywhere in helpers/pdf/; the only size checks (MIN_IMAGE_PX 150, MIN_IMAGE_BYTES 8192) are minimums applied after decode

trace.description: the CLI takes the source PDF path and drives the engine chain; no input-size or page-count gate before parse
returns [page.get_pixmap(matrix).tobytes('png') for page in doc] — every page's raster materialized in one list, unbounded in page count x dimensions
MuPDF renders the uncompressed page surface (width x height x 4 bytes) inside the vendored parser, before any repo-side gate

evidence.description: render_pages has no page-count or dimension guard; the pixmap list is built eagerly
pymupdf.open + Pixmap(doc, xref) decode with only post-decode minimum-size checks (MIN_IMAGE_BYTES 8192)
_image_ok checks MIN_IMAGE_PX 150 / MIN_IMAGE_BYTES 8192 on the already-decoded pixmap — minimums, not ceilings

conditions.value: third-party-origin newsletter/report PDFs (the SEC-6 capture domain) are semi-attacker-controlled: a hostile PDF reaching Reports/ or the OCR corpus reaches the parser
no input cap configured: pdf_conv_md exposes no --max-pages/--max-page-dims flag; nothing in helpers/pdf/ caps input size, page count or page dimensions before render

blockers: end-to-end measurement through the pdf_conv_md CLI on the Reports corpus not yet run: the amplification was demonstrated on the render path directly (synthetic hostile PDF), not through the full CLI with the operator's corpus
the remediation decision (input cap defaults) is an operator call: the tracked Reports corpus tops out at 0.8 MB / 28 pages, so a cap must not break the real workload

validation_plan.local: run pdf_conv_md end-to-end on a synthetic hostile PDF (819 B, 6000x6000pt MediaBox) through each engine path (pdf_local / liteparse / teleocr) and measure peak RSS; then decide --max-pages / --max-page-dim defaults against the 28-page, 0.8 MB Reports maximum and re-measure
